request.job_description: We are hiring a Frontend Engineer to build accessible, production-quality product UI using React and TypeScript. You will own features end to end, collaborate with design and backend engineers, write tested components, and ensure our interfaces meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards. Experience with performance optimization, design systems and automated testing is expected.

transcript.question: Can you walk me through how you would build a reusable modal dialog component in React with TypeScript?
transcript.answer: Sure, I would make a component called Modal and pass in props like isOpen and children. I would use useState to show and hide it. For TypeScript I would just type the props, or use any if it gets complicated. Then I would style it with CSS so it appears in the middle of the screen.

transcript.question: How would you make that modal accessible to keyboard and screen reader users?
transcript.answer: I think you add alt text and maybe some aria labels. Accessibility is mostly about making sure images have alt text, I believe. I usually run it through a tool at the end if there is time, but I have not really worked with screen readers myself.

transcript.question: A page in your app has become slow after a recent release. How would you investigate?
transcript.answer: I would probably look at the code and see if anything looks slow. Maybe add React.memo to all the components, since that makes things faster. I have heard of the profiler but I have not used it much.

transcript.question: Tell me about how you test your frontend code.
transcript.answer: On my last team we had some tests but I did not write many of them. I mostly tested manually by clicking around in the browser. I know Jest exists and that it is used for testing.

transcript.question: Describe a time you disagreed with a designer or teammate about a UI decision and how it was resolved.
transcript.answer: There was a time the designer wanted something that was hard to build. I told them it was not possible and we just did something simpler. It worked out fine I think. The team was generally happy.
